definitions.explanation: Wood that has been carried along by a river or washed up on a shore. Often used decoratively in aquariums and gardens.

examples.japanese: {浜辺|はまべ}に{流木|りゅうぼく}があった。
examples.english: There was driftwood on the beach.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}の{後|あと}、{大量|たいりょう}の{流木|りゅうぼく}が{海岸|かいがん}に{流|なが}れ{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: After the typhoon, a huge amount of driftwood washed up on the coast.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{拾|ひろ}ってきた{流木|りゅうぼく}で{素敵|すてき}なテーブルを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: He made a beautiful table out of driftwood he had picked up.

notes:
Compound of {流|りゅう} (flow) + {木|ぼく} (wood). Refers to wood that has floated downstream or been carried by the sea. Frequently associated with beach scenes and natural disasters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {流木|りゅうぼく}が{流|なが}れ{着|つ}く: driftwood washes ashore
- {流木|りゅうぼく}を{拾|ひろ}う: to pick up driftwood
- {流木|りゅうぼく}の{家具|かぐ}: driftwood furniture
- アクアリウム{用|よう}の{流木|りゅうぼく}: driftwood for aquariums
